title: 5 Minute Nacho Cheese Sauce
steps: Whisk the butter and flour in a small pot over medium heat until bubbly and foamy, then keep whisking for about 60 seconds without letting it brown.
Whisk in the milk, turn the heat up slightly, and bring to a simmer, whisking, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Turn off the heat.
Stir in the cheddar one handful at a time until melted. Put it back over low heat if needed to help it melt, but don't overheat.
Stir in the salt and chili powder, taste, and adjust. Add a splash of milk if it's too thick.
notes: Makes about 6 servings of 1/4 cup. Use medium cheddar (sharp can go grainy) and shred it from a block. Best eaten fresh; leftovers keep 3 to 4 days, reheat low and slow with a splash of milk. Mild on purpose, so add jalapeno brine, Rotel, or more spice if you want it bolder. No fitting category on the site, so I put it under Sides.

title: Air Fryer Chicken Chimichangas
ingredients: Avocado oil (for frying, brushing, or spraying)
steps: Mix the chicken, cream cheese, green chiles, salsa, cumin, garlic powder, garlic salt, and cheddar until well combined, with no cream cheese clumps.
Spoon the filling into the center of each tortilla, fold in the ends, and roll up like a burrito. Place seam side down.

Air fryer: Preheat to 390°F for 3 min. Brush or spray all sides with oil and place seam side down. Cook 4 min, flip, and cook 4-5 min more until browned. If a seam opens, secure with a toothpick or cook 1 more min seam side down.
Oven: Place seam side down on a greased baking sheet. Brush or spray well with oil. Bake at 400°F for 20-25 min until golden brown.
Skillet: Heat enough oil to cover the bottom of a skillet over medium heat. Cook seam side down 2-3 min until golden, then turn and cook all sides until crisp.
notes: Makes 6, about 15 minutes. The filling can be made up to 3 days ahead. Wrap and cook right before serving so the tortillas stay crisp. Serve on lettuce with salsa, sour cream, and cheese sauce.

title: Air Fryer Garlic Butter Steak Bites and Potatoes
ingredients: Olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and dried parsley, for the potatoes (no amounts given)
Salt, pepper and garlic powder (no amounts given)
Steak seasoning (Kinder's Prime Steak Seasoning), amount not given
steps: Wash the potatoes and cut into small cubes.
Toss the potatoes in olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and dried parsley.
Air fry the potatoes at 400°F for about 20 minutes, shaking a couple of times. Set aside when done.
Cut the steak into 1 inch cubes and coat with olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder and steak seasoning.
Air fry the steak bites at 400°F for about 7 minutes (about medium).
Melt the butter and stir in the minced garlic and dried parsley.
Pour the garlic butter over the steak bites and serve over the potatoes.
notes: About 37 minutes total. Preheat the air fryer if it has that feature for a better sear. Pull the steak at 145°F; some reviewers found 7 minutes dry and did 4 to 6. Two 8 to 10 ounce steaks feed a family of four with the potatoes. Source gives no amounts for the seasonings.

title: Air Fryer Pork Belly Bites
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds pork belly (skin on or off), cut into 2 inch cubes
Teriyaki or sweet chili sauce, for dipping (optional)
steps: Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper and olive oil in a large bowl.
Add the pork belly and toss until every piece is coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for 4 to 5 minutes, then add the pork in a single layer.
Air fry at 400°F for 15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown with some charred edges.
Serve warm, on their own or with dipping sauce.
notes: Serves 4 to 6. The pieces shrink a lot, so cut them big. Best eaten right away; leftovers keep 3 days and reheat in the air fryer at 350°F for 5 minutes. The source doesn't give an amount for the pepper.

title: Air Fryer White Fish with Garlic and Lemon Pepper
ingredients: 12 ounces tilapia fillets or other white fish (2 fillets, 6 ounces each)
Kosher or sea salt, to taste
Fresh cracked black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the air fryer to 360°F for 5 minutes. Rinse the fillets and pat dry.
Spray or coat the fish with olive oil spray and season both sides with the garlic powder, lemon pepper, onion powder, salt and pepper.
Lay perforated parchment in the basket (or spray the basket well) and lightly spray it so the fish doesn't stick.
Put the fish on the paper with a few lemon wedges alongside.
Air fry at 360°F for about 6 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes with a fork. Time depends on thickness.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve warm with the toasted lemon wedges.
notes: Serves 2, about 15 minutes. Thicker fish like cod or halibut needs 1 to 2 more minutes. If the air fryer is already hot or you're cooking multiple batches, cut the time by a few minutes. Reviewers had good results with cod at 11 minutes and rockfish at 12.

title: Apple Cider Pork Chops
steps: Pat the pork chops dry with a paper towel and sprinkle both sides with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a 10 inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Cook the chops about 4 minutes per side, until golden brown. Remove from the skillet.
In the same skillet, add the apple cider and brown sugar and cook until reduced by about half to a thick, syrupy glaze. Stir in the mustard and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the glaze over the pork chops to serve.
notes: Serves 4, about 25 minutes. Scrape up the brown bits when making the sauce for the most flavor. Good with rice and green beans. The source doesn't say how long to cook the chops through (4 minutes per side is for browning); check for 145°F.

title: Authentic Mexican Rice
ingredients: 2 teaspoons granulated tomato bouillon (or cubes; chicken bouillon works)
steps: Rinse the rice in a fine mesh strainer until the water runs clear.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the rice and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until lightly golden all over, about 10 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, garlic and onion and stir. Add the tomato bouillon, salt, carrot, peas, water and the serranos if using.
Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low, and cook about 20 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Remove from the heat and rest 5 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork.
notes: Serves 6, about 35 minutes. Serranos go in whole for flavor, not heat; take them out before serving. Don't stir while cooking and do rest the rice before fluffing. For brown rice add 1/2 cup more water and cook 40 minutes. Can be made a day ahead; reheat covered with a splash of water.

title: Baked Chicken Parmesan
ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 8 ounces each), sliced in half lengthwise to make 8 cutlets
steps: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Spray a large baking sheet.
Mix the breadcrumbs and parmesan in a bowl. Melt the butter in another bowl. Brush the butter lightly onto each cutlet, dip into the breadcrumbs, press to coat, and set on the baking sheet.
Spray the tops lightly with oil and bake 25 minutes, until golden.
Spoon about 1 tablespoon marinara over each cutlet and top with about 1 1/2 tablespoons mozzarella.
Bake 5 more minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling. Garnish with basil or parsley.
notes: Serves 8 (1 cutlet each), about 40 minutes. Brushing with butter instead of an egg wash keeps it lighter. Good over pasta, zucchini noodles or with a salad, or on a roll as a sandwich. Freezer friendly.

title: Baked Rigatoni with Beef
ingredients: 1 (28 ounce) can crushed tomatoes with basil
1 pound part-skim mozzarella, cut into 1 inch cubes
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and spray a 9x13 baking dish. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Warm 1/2 tablespoon oil in a saute pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef, season lightly, and brown 5 to 7 minutes, breaking it up. Move the beef to a plate and drain the pan.
Reduce to medium, add the remaining 2 tablespoons oil and the onion, and cook about 8 minutes until very soft. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute. Stir in the tomato paste.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth, salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, about 15 minutes. Stir in the basil, cook 5 more minutes, then stir in the beef.
Meanwhile cook the rigatoni 8 to 9 minutes until just al dente. Drain and return to the pot, add the meat sauce, and stir well.
Pour into the baking dish and top with the cubed mozzarella.
Bake 30 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly. Garnish with fresh basil and serve warm.
notes: Serves 8, about 1 hour. Use all the sauce so the noodles stay tender. Italian sausage can replace the beef. Freezes up to 2 months; thaw 12 hours, then bake covered at 350°F for 30 minutes and uncovered 10 to 15 more. Serve with extra sauce, since freezing dries it out a bit.

title: Bourbon Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken (thighs or breasts)
2 tablespoons cornstarch (only if stir frying the chicken)
1/4 cup (2 ounces) apple sauce (or apple, pineapple or orange juice)
1/4 cup brown sugar (or honey or maple syrup)
1 teaspoon minced or grated fresh ginger
Garnish: 2 green onions, chopped, and 2 teaspoons toasted sesame seeds (optional)
steps: Heat the grill or oven if using one.
Whisk all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl.

Cook the chicken one of these ways, then keep it warm. Grill: toss with oil, salt and pepper, grill on medium high 3 to 4 minutes per side, rest 5 minutes, cut into bite-size pieces. Bake: oil, salt and pepper, bake at 425°F about 18 minutes, rest 5 minutes, cut up. Stir fry: cut into bite-size pieces, shake in a bag with 2 tablespoons cornstarch and 1/2 teaspoon salt, saute in oil on medium high in two batches, 4 to 5 minutes.
Heat a skillet on medium high, add the sauce, and cook, stirring, until it boils and thickens, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir to coat. Lower the heat and cook 2 more minutes until heated through. Thin with a tablespoon or two of water or juice if too thick.
Serve over rice and garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Serves 4. About 20 minutes. Sauce can be made ahead. Leftovers keep 2 to 3 days. A shortcut is to heat the sauce and stir in chopped rotisserie chicken. One reviewer said it tastes more like BBQ sauce than the mall version.

title: Boursin Cheese Pasta
ingredients: 1 5.3-ounce package garlic & fine herbs Boursin cheese
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt (plus more to taste)
8 ounces bow tie pasta (farfalle), or fusilli or rotini
Grated parmesan and more basil, for garnish (optional)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. In a 9x13 ceramic casserole dish, put the Boursin in the middle and surround it with the tomatoes, red onion and garlic.
Drizzle with the olive oil, sprinkle with oregano, salt and pepper, and gently toss the vegetables to coat.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the tomatoes burst and the onion softens.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta. Reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

Stir the cheese and tomatoes together in the dish, gently squishing the tomatoes. Stir in the basil, then add the pasta and toss to coat. Add pasta water a little at a time to thin the sauce (1/4 cup was enough).
Serve right away with more basil and parmesan.
notes: Serves 4, about 40 minutes. To add chicken: season two 8 ounce chicken breasts with salt and pepper, set them on either side of the Boursin in the dish, bake about 35 minutes until 165°F. Leftovers keep up to 4 days. Good with spinach, sausage or shrimp added.

title: Brown Sugar Glazed Carrots
steps: Combine the carrots, water, butter and brown sugar in a pan over medium-high heat and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to low, and cook about 6 minutes.
Keeping it covered, turn the heat to high and cook, stirring now and then, until the liquid reduces to a glossy glaze and the carrots are fork-tender, another 5 to 8 minutes. Don't overcook.
Remove from the heat and season with salt and pepper.
notes: Serves 4, about 20 minutes. Whole carrots, peeled and cut into even sticks, cook more evenly than baby carrots according to one reviewer. Oven: 350°F covered for 1 hour. Slow cooker: HIGH 2 to 3 hours. Leftovers keep 2 to 3 days.

title: Cashew Chicken with Rice
ingredients: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1 inch cubes
Garnish: 1/2 cup chopped cashews, 2 green onions sliced, sriracha (optional)
steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Stir together all the sauce ingredients and set aside.
Mix the cornstarch and salt in a medium bowl. Pat the chicken dry, cube it, and toss in the cornstarch mixture.
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and add the vegetable and sesame oils. Cook the chicken 4 minutes until lightly browned, then remove.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the broccoli, carrots and red pepper about 5 minutes until barely tender. Return the chicken to the pan.
Pour in the sauce and cook a few more minutes. Add salt if needed.
Serve over the rice, topped with cashews, green onions and sriracha.
notes: Frozen veggies work in a pinch. Skip the nuts to make it nut-free. For gluten-free, use tamari or coconut aminos (go lightly with aminos).

title: Cheesy Scalloped Potatoes and Ham
ingredients: 2 cups nonfat milk (plus up to 1/4 cup more if the sauce is too thick)
2 1/4 cups freshly shredded cheddar cheese, divided
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 13x9 baking pan with cooking spray.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Scrub the potatoes and boil them whole for about 20 minutes. Remove and let cool until easy to handle.
Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, whisking constantly, until golden, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the milk and cook, stirring often, until thickened, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in 2 cups of the cheddar, and season with salt and pepper.
Peel the potatoes and slice into 1/8 inch rounds.
Layer 1/3 of the potatoes in the dish, overlapping, and season with salt and pepper. Top with half the ham and about 1/3 of the cheese sauce.
Repeat with a second layer of potatoes, ham and sauce. Finish with the last of the potatoes and pour the remaining sauce over the top, spreading to cover.
Sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 cup cheddar and 1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon paprika.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbly. Garnish with chives and serve right away.
notes: Serves 6 as a main, 8 to 10 as a side. Boiling the potatoes first is what keeps them evenly creamy. Can be baked ahead, cooled, wrapped, and refrigerated 2 to 3 days; reheat at 350°F for 25 to 35 minutes. Freezes up to 4 months. Source gives no amounts for salt and pepper.

title: Creamy Chicken Pesto Pasta
ingredients: 1 pound asparagus, ends trimmed and cut into 2 inch pieces
steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water according to the package. Don't rinse it.

Cut the chicken breasts in half lengthwise and season with 1/2 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat and cook the chicken 3 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Add 2 tablespoons oil and the asparagus to the same pan and saute 2 to 3 minutes until crisp tender.
Add the cream, bring to a simmer, and cook 3 minutes. Stir in the pesto, add the chicken, and cook 2 minutes. Don't boil or the sauce can separate. Season with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Add the cooked pasta, stir to coat, and serve right away. Garnish with basil or parsley.
notes: Serves 8 as written (about 30 minutes). Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days; reheat on low with a splash of cream or broth. Store-bought pesto works fine. Rotisserie chicken can replace the chicken breasts (skip the chicken-cooking step).

title: Creamy Chicken Wild Rice Soup
ingredients: 2 cups thinly sliced celery (3 to 4 stalks)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large stockpot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, celery, mushrooms, garlic, thyme, rosemary, oregano, salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 10 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir to coat. Cook, stirring constantly, 2 minutes, scraping up anything stuck to the pan.
Stir in the chicken stock, water, wild rice and chicken. Bring to a simmer, reduce to low, cover, and cook 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. Check that the rice is done.
Stir in the cream, taste, and add more salt and pepper as needed. Keep warm until serving.
notes: Makes 8 servings, about 1 hour 15 minutes. Cook time doesn't include cooking the chicken. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge.

title: Creamy Garlic Mushrooms and Bacon
ingredients: 26 ounces brown mushrooms, washed and patted dry
1/4 cup dry white wine or chicken broth
Salt and pepper, a pinch of each
steps: Fry the bacon in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat until crispy. Move to a paper towel lined plate with a slotted spoon.
In the same pan, melt the butter. Add the mushrooms, drizzle with the oil, scrape up the browned bits, and fry 2 to 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in the wine or broth and let it reduce 2 minutes, stirring now and then. Preheat the broiler.

Add the garlic and stir about 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in the cream, parsley and thyme, lower the heat, and simmer gently 4 to 5 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir the bacon back in and top with the mozzarella and parmesan.
Broil 3 to 5 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly. Serve warm.
notes: Serves 8 as a side, about 40 minutes. Use a wide pan so the mushrooms brown. Season at the end since the bacon and parmesan are salty. Works over steak, chicken or pasta.

title: Creamy Mushroom Wild Rice
ingredients: 1 cup wild rice (quick-cook wild rice blend, see notes)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft.
Add the garlic and stir 1 minute. Season with salt, pepper and Italian seasoning.
Add the broth and rice, bring to a boil, then reduce to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand covered 5 minutes.
Uncover and stir in the cream and parmesan until the cheese melts.
notes: Serves 6, about 25 minutes. The 15 minute time is for a quick-cook wild rice blend. Regular wild rice can take about 45 minutes, so check the package. Long grain white rice, basmati or jasmine also work.

title: Crispy Sheet Pan Gnocchi and Veggies
ingredients: 1 (12 ounce) bag mixed baby bell peppers (or 2 medium bell peppers)
1 pound fresh, shelf-stable, or frozen potato gnocchi
2 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for drizzling
Grated Pecorino Romano or parmesan, for serving
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
In a large bowl, combine the bell peppers cut into 1 inch chunks, the red onion halved and thinly sliced, the garlic minced, and 1 teaspoon coarsely chopped rosemary leaves.
Add the gnocchi (straight from the package, no boiling), tomatoes, salt and a few grinds of pepper. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil and toss gently. Spread in an even layer on the baking sheet.
Roast, stirring halfway, until the gnocchi are plump and the vegetables are tender and browning, 18 to 20 minutes.
Right out of the oven, tear the burrata and basil over the top. Sprinkle with Pecorino or parmesan and red pepper flakes, and drizzle with more olive oil if you like.
notes: Serves 4, about 25 minutes. The ingredient list says 1/4 teaspoon salt but the step says 1/2, so I used 1/2. Roasted gnocchi gets crispy outside and chewy inside rather than light. Leftovers keep up to 4 days.

title: Crockpot Chicken and Rice
ingredients: 1 cup long-grain brown rice (no other kind of rice)
1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs
1/2 cup freshly grated sharp cheddar, divided
steps: Rinse the rice several times. Boil 2 cups of the broth, add the rice, cook 10 minutes, then drain.

Coat a 5-quart or larger slow cooker with nonstick spray. Add the rice, carrots, shallot and Dijon and stir. Lay the chicken on top and sprinkle with the garlic powder, thyme, salt and pepper. Pour in 2 1/2 cups broth.
Cover and cook on HIGH 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the chicken is cooked through.

Remove the chicken to a plate and cover. Stir the rice mixture, re-cover, and cook on high until the rice is tender, about 1 to 1 1/2 more hours. Splash in some of the remaining broth if it looks dry.
Stir in the peas and Greek yogurt. Dice the chicken and stir it in with 1/4 cup of the cheddar. Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top, cover a few minutes until melted, and serve with parsley.
notes: Serves 4. Must cook on HIGH (low gives mushy rice). Thaw the chicken first. Pull the chicken at 160°F. Slow cookers vary a lot, so plan on extra time the first go; rice can take longer. Leftovers keep 4 days, freeze up to 3 months. Reviews are mixed on how the rice turns out.

title: Denver Omelet Egg Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a muffin tin (silicone releases easiest).
In a medium bowl, beat the eggs, cream, baking powder, salt and pepper until fully combined.
Stir in the ham, cheese, onion and bell pepper until evenly distributed.
Scoop 1/4 cup of the mixture into each muffin cup.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until set and a toothpick comes out clean.
notes: Makes 12, about 25 minutes. Fridge up to 5 days; reheat in the microwave in 15 second bursts. Freezes well: cool completely, freeze on a plate, then bag; reheat in 30 second bursts. Source says the salt amount covers the pepper too, so the pepper amount is unspecified. Pepper jack instead of cheddar adds spice.

title: Garlic Butter Chicken Bites with Lemon Asparagus
ingredients: 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized chunks
1/2 cup butter, divided (1/4 cup for the chicken, 1/4 cup for the sauce)
1 teaspoon Italian seasoning or Herbes de Provence
Chicken seasoning: 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper, 2 teaspoons onion powder
steps: Season the chicken chunks with the salt, pepper and onion powder and let sit on a plate.
Blanch the trimmed asparagus in boiling water 2 minutes, then move to ice water. Drain. Skip this if the asparagus is skinny.

Melt 1/4 cup butter with the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the chicken on all sides in batches, so it doesn't steam. Lower the heat, add 1 teaspoon garlic and the Italian seasoning, and cook 1 minute. Move the chicken to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the remaining teaspoon of garlic, and deglaze with the chicken broth. Simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the remaining 1/4 cup butter, lemon juice, hot sauce and parsley.
Add the asparagus and toss 2 minutes. Push it aside, return the chicken, and stir 1 minute to reheat.
Garnish with more parsley, pepper flakes and lemon slices and serve right away.
notes: Serves 4, about 30 minutes. Good over rice or cauliflower rice. Broccoli, green beans or zucchini can replace the asparagus. A splash of white wine can replace some of the broth. Chicken bites are done in 5 to 6 minutes (165°F).

title: Garlic Mushroom Chicken Bites
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, cut into 1 inch pieces
1 tablespoon seeded, chopped green bell pepper
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, season with salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder and paprika, and sear until browned and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes. Move to a plate and keep warm.
Heat the remaining oil and 1 tablespoon butter in the same pan. Add the mushrooms and cook, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes until just starting to brown and soften.
Add the remaining butter. When melted, saute the shallot and bell pepper about 3 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for about 30 seconds.
Return the chicken with its juices and toss to coat. Cook 1 to 2 more minutes until the vegetables are soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Taste, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve warm with the parsley.
notes: Serves 4 to 6, about 30 minutes. Chicken is done at 165°F. Add chili powder, red pepper flakes or sriracha for heat. Good on toothpicks as an appetizer.

title: Garlic Parmesan Chicken Thighs
ingredients: 3 cloves garlic, minced (or 2 teaspoons garlic powder)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F and spray a 9x13 baking dish with nonstick spray.
In one shallow dish, mix the olive oil and garlic. In a second, mix the bread crumbs, parmesan, Italian seasoning and oregano.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Dip each thigh in the oil, then dredge in the crumb mixture, and place in the baking dish.
Bake 30 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F.
Broil 2 minutes to brown the cheese. Garnish with parsley.
notes: About 45 minutes. If you use garlic powder instead of fresh, mix it into the crumbs, not the oil. Some reviewers found the thighs needed up to 45 minutes to reach temperature, and some had leftover crumb mixture. Works with bone-in thighs (longer time) and in the air fryer (about 15 minutes).

title: Garlic Parmesan Roasted Carrots
ingredients: 4 large cloves garlic, minced (or 1 tablespoon minced garlic)
Salt and pepper, a pinch of each to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and lightly grease a baking sheet.
Spread the carrots on the sheet in a single layer with a little space between them. Add the olive oil, garlic, parmesan, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper and toss to coat.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, tossing halfway, until fork tender and golden.
Serve right away, topped with parsley.
notes: Serves 6, about 30 minutes. Dry the carrots well and cut them evenly so they crisp. Air fryer: 390°F for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking halfway. Best fresh; leftovers keep 3 to 4 days and reheat at 400°F.

title: Glazed Ham and Cheese Sliders (Hawaiian Rolls)
ingredients: 1 package (12 count) King's Hawaiian Sweet Rolls
12 slices smoked ham (about 1/2 pound, thinly sliced or shaved)
12 slices Monterey Jack or Colby Jack cheese (about 1/4 pound)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Melt the butter with the brown sugar, Worcestershire and mustard in a small pot, stirring until smooth.
Keeping the rolls attached, slice them in half horizontally. Brush the glaze generously onto both cut sides, saving a little for the tops.
Put the bottom halves in a 9x13 baking dish. Layer the ham, then the cheese. Add the tops and brush with the leftover glaze. Sprinkle with poppy seeds if using.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 25 minutes, until the cheese is melted.
Slice and serve, with warmed raspberry preserves on the side if you like.
notes: Makes 12, about 35 minutes. Can be assembled the night before; add a few minutes baking from cold. Cut the bottom half a bit thicker so it doesn't get soggy. A reviewer suggested adding the glaze right before baking if making ahead. Leftovers are good cold or microwaved. Works with turkey instead of ham.

title: Grilled Bruschetta Chicken
ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, pounded to an even thickness (1 inch or less)
steps: In a large bowl, toss the chicken with the oil, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Grill over medium-high heat 6 to 8 minutes per side, until cooked through.
Meanwhile, stir the tomatoes, lemon juice, basil, salt and pepper together in a bowl.
Top each chicken breast with a slice of mozzarella and grill about 1 more minute until melted.
Top with the tomato basil mixture and serve right away.
notes: Serves 4, about 30 minutes. The tomato topping can be made ahead and kept in the fridge. The source's written steps skip the salt, but the ingredient list calls for 1/2 teaspoon, so I added it to step 1.

title: Hot Chicken Philly Cheesesteak Dip
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Season the chicken with salt and pepper on both sides.
Spray a grill pan or large skillet with cooking spray and cook the chicken over high heat about 1 minute per side, until cooked through. Slice thin and set aside.
Spray more oil in the pan and saute the onions and peppers over medium-low heat 5 to 6 minutes until soft.
Combine all the ingredients in a medium bowl.
Put in an oven-proof dish and bake 20 to 25 minutes, until hot and the cheese is melted.
notes: Makes 12 servings of 1/4 cup, about 45 minutes. Can be assembled a day ahead and refrigerated before baking. Serve with toasted baguette slices, bagel thins, pretzel thins, tortilla chips or veggies. The author tried Greek yogurt in place of sour cream but preferred the light sour cream.

title: Lighter Broccoli Beef
ingredients: 1 1/4 pounds flank or sirloin steak, sliced very thin against the grain
1/2 cup + 2 tablespoons reduced-sodium tamari or soy sauce, divided
2 1/2 tablespoons cornstarch (or gluten free flour), divided
1/2 teaspoon ground ginger (or 1 teaspoon ginger paste)
steps: In a zip bag, combine the sliced steak, 2 tablespoons tamari and 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Seal, squish to coat, and refrigerate while you prep.

Whisk together the remaining 1/2 cup tamari, remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons cornstarch, chicken broth, brown sugar, 2 tablespoons water, rice vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and chili flakes. Set aside.
Heat a large wok or nonstick skillet on high. Add 1/4 cup water, and when it simmers add the broccoli and stir fry 2 to 3 minutes until crisp tender. Move to a plate.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil until very hot. Add half the beef in a single layer, let it sit 30 seconds to brown, then stir fry until barely cooked through (a little pink is fine). Move to the plate. Repeat with the remaining oil and beef.
Pour the sauce into the wok and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return the beef and broccoli, simmer about 1 minute until heated through, and serve over rice.
notes: Serves 4, about 25 minutes. Have everything ready before you start; the cooking only takes 5 to 7 minutes. Gluten free if you use tamari and gluten free broth.

title: Loaded Reese’s Peanut Butter Dip
ingredients: 2/3 cup mini peanut butter cups, chopped
Extra mini peanut butter cups, chopped (topping)
steps: Mix the softened cream cheese, peanut butter, brown sugar, vanilla, and salt in a large bowl with an electric mixer until fully combined.
Fold in the Cool Whip until combined.
Stir in the mini Reese’s Pieces and chopped peanut butter cups.
Transfer to a serving dish.
Top with more Reese’s Pieces and chopped peanut butter cups right before serving.
notes: Serves 10, about 15 minutes. Serve with graham crackers, pretzels, vanilla wafers, apple slices, or strawberries. Chill 20-30 min for a thicker dip. Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Do not leave out more than 2 hours. Do not freeze.

title: Moroccan Chicken
ingredients: 1/4 cup Land O Lakes Cinnamon Sugar Butter Spread
1 small (1/2 cup) yellow onion, thinly sliced
1 medium (1 cup) red bell pepper, cut into strips
1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1 inch pieces
Cooked rice or couscous, for serving (optional)
steps: Melt the cinnamon sugar butter spread in a 12 inch skillet until sizzling. Add the onion and cook over medium-high heat 2 to 3 minutes until crisp-tender. Add the bell pepper and cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
Add the chicken, garlic, salt and cayenne. Cook, stirring occasionally, 5 to 7 minutes until the chicken is browned and no longer pink.
Add the orange juice and raisins and cook, stirring, 1 to 2 minutes until heated through. Stir in the cilantro.
Serve right away over rice or couscous.
notes: Serves 4, about 25 minutes. Uses cinnamon sugar butter spread, a specific product; if you can't find it, use regular butter with a pinch of cinnamon and sugar (my substitution, not from the source).

title: Oatmeal Cinnamon French Toast
ingredients: 4 thick slices day-old Italian bread (or bread of choice)
1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, plus extra for serving
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla and spices. Add the bread and move the slices around gently so they soak up the mixture evenly.
Put the oats in a shallow dish.
Melt the butter over medium heat in a large nonstick pan.
Coat the soaked bread slices on both sides with the oats.
Fry over medium-high heat until golden brown on both sides.
Serve with extra cinnamon, fresh berries and plenty of maple syrup.
notes: Serves 2, about 10 minutes. Slightly crunchy, sweet and spicy. Reviewers made it with oatmeal bread and with a non-dairy milk.

title: One Pan Chicken and Potatoes
ingredients: 8 chicken thighs and drumsticks, about 2 1/2 pounds
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Dry the chicken and potatoes well with a paper towel and place in a 9x13 rimmed baking dish.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, 7 spice, paprika, salt and pepper. Drizzle over the chicken, add the potatoes, and use your hands to coat everything.
Bake uncovered 55 to 65 minutes, until the potatoes are fork tender and the chicken is cooked through. Broil 3 to 5 minutes more for color if needed.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then garnish with parsley.
notes: Serves 4. Leftovers keep up to 4 days. Chicken freezes well but the potatoes do not. If the potatoes aren't done when the chicken is, quarter them next time. Don't have 7 spice? Swap in Italian seasoning, Cajun or lemon pepper.

title: Pan Seared Halibut with Lemon Butter Sauce
ingredients: 4 halibut fillets, 6 ounces each (1 1/2 pounds total)
steps: Pat the fillets completely dry with paper towels. Season both sides with the garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes.
Add the fillets in a single layer (in batches if needed) and sear without moving for 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges are opaque.
Flip and cook 2 to 4 minutes, until cooked through. Remove and cover with foil to keep warm.
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the butter to the same pan and cook 2 to 3 minutes, stirring now and then, until browned and nutty-smelling.
Squeeze in the juice of both lemon halves, bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, until reduced by half. It will still be thin.
Drizzle a little sauce on each plate, set the fish on top, and drizzle more sauce over it.
notes: Serves 4, about 15 to 20 minutes. Fish is done at 135 to 140°F. A non-stick pan works best. Keep the heat low for the sauce; several reviewers had it burn or split when the pan was too hot. Other white fish (cod, haddock, snapper) work too. Best fresh; leftovers keep 3 to 4 days.

title: Parmesan Pasta with Broccoli and Mushrooms
ingredients: 10 ounces spaghetti (gluten free in the original)
Seasoned salt and pepper (homemade blend of salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder; amounts not given)
steps: Boil a large pot of water. Add the broccoli and cook 2 to 3 minutes until crisp tender. Scoop it out, drain, and set aside.
Return the water to a boil, cook the pasta al dente, reserve about 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile, heat a 12 inch skillet over medium-high heat. Melt 2 tablespoons butter and saute the mushrooms and shallot 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown and tender. Season with seasoned salt and pepper once browned.
Put the mushrooms, pasta, remaining 4 tablespoons butter and the parmesan in the pasta pot. Drizzle in some pasta water and stir until creamy, adding more as needed.
Add the broccoli and plenty of seasoned salt and pepper, stir once more, and serve.
notes: Serves 6, about 30 minutes. Spread the mushrooms out so they brown instead of steaming. The seasoned salt amounts aren't given; the source links a homemade recipe for it. Any pasta works.

title: Smoked Beef and Cheese Sliders
ingredients: Garlic (powder, salt, fresh, frozen, or minced)
steps: Cut chuck roast into large chunks.
Coat with mustard as a binder, then season with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and all-purpose seasoning.
Sear on the stove.
Crockpot with 1/2 cup beef stock: 5-6 hrs on high or 8-10 on low. Re-add seasonings.
Last 1/2 hr, add butter and brown sugar to each chunk.
Shred with some of the juice.
Toast the middles of the buns in the air fryer, middle side up.
Melt 5 tbsp butter with garlic. Brush half on the bottom layer of buns.
Layer provolone, meat, BBQ drizzle, then frizzled onions.
Bake at 350°F for 15 min.
notes: Air fryer toasting: on 4 slices, 3 dark.

title: Stove Top Beef Stew
ingredients: 1 teaspoon dried rosemary, crushed between your fingers
1 large shallot or small onion, finely chopped
1 1/2 pounds stew meat, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
steps: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the thyme and rosemary and cook 30 seconds.
Add the carrots, celery and shallot, season with salt and pepper, and saute about 10 minutes until browned and tender.
Add the mushrooms and saute 7 to 9 minutes, until their liquid cooks off. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the stew meat, red pepper flakes and more salt and pepper, and saute 8 to 10 minutes until browned.
Mash the butter and flour together with a fork, stir it into the pot, and cook 1 minute.
Stream in the beef broth, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a simmer on high, add the bay leaves, cover, turn to low, and simmer 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Remove the lid and simmer gently another 1 1/2 hours, until the meat is tender and the stew is thick. Put the lid back on if it reduces too fast.
Adjust the salt and pepper, add the peas, and simmer 2 minutes. Remove the bay leaves and serve over mashed potatoes.
notes: Serves 6, about 4 hours. Chop the vegetables very fine so they melt into the gravy. Freezes well; thaw in the fridge and reheat on the stove.
